transcript.answer: I can't confirm this for Lore specifically, because I have no access to the repository's files and don't know of any Lore documentation on it. The usual cause in OpenTelemetry is that an instrument created at module import time comes from the global meter before the SDK's MeterProvider has been configured. At that point the global provider is a no-op, so the instrument is a no-op and its recordings are dropped. If the provider is set later during app startup, an instrument already created may stay bound to the no-op and never record. The usual fix is to create instruments lazily after the provider is initialized, or to pass the provider in explicitly. I can't say whether Lore's code or docs give this exact reason.

judgements.reason: The answer gives the right mechanism and fix: an instrument created before the MeterProvider is set is a no-op, and instruments should be created lazily. But it hedges that the instrument only 'may' stay bound, never mentions the missing proxy meter, and disclaims knowledge of Lore.
